input.strategy_title: FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Public-sector deals require the model serving stack to run on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules. Today KServe
components and the serving data plane link non-validated crypto libraries in
several images, and we have no compliance evidence package. Certification
involves an external accredited laboratory (historical turnaround: six to nine
months) and mandatory security review board sign-off at defined milestones —
these human and third-party gates dominate the schedule regardless of
engineering speed.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | All serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto in the request path). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A compliance evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security review board to the external certification lab. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | CI enforces FIPS regressions: a gating check fails any serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Platform Operator

## Out of Scope

- FIPS posture for workbenches, pipelines, and training (separate strategies)
- Common Criteria certification

## Open Questions

None on scope — but note that lab scheduling and review-board cadence are
externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort.

# FIPS 140-3 crypto remediation of KServe serving-stack images

## Description

This epic makes every KServe serving-stack image — the control-plane components
and the serving data plane — run correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters
using validated cryptographic modules, with no non-validated crypto in the
request path. It covers the crypto audit of the images, remediation of every
non-validated crypto linkage found, verification on a FIPS-enabled cluster, and
a gating CI check that prevents regressions.

## Scope

- Audit all KServe serving-stack images (control-plane components and serving
  data-plane images) to produce a module inventory: every image, every linked
  cryptographic library, and its FIPS validation status.
- Remediate every non-validated crypto linkage in the request path: rebuild the
  affected images against validated cryptographic modules and FIPS-capable
  toolchains and base images.
- Rebuild and publish the remediated images through the existing Konflux build
  pipeline for KServe.
- Verify serving behavior on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster: model deployment
  and inference requests through the InferenceService request path.
- Wire a gating CI check that fails any KServe serving-stack build that
  reintroduces non-validated crypto usage (blocking image-scan step in the
  build pipeline).
- Preserve serving behavior on non-FIPS clusters and keep previously released
  image tags deployable as the rollback path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A module inventory exists that lists every KServe serving-stack image and
  each linked cryptographic library with its validation status.
- An automated scan of the rebuilt images finds no non-validated cryptographic
  library linked in the request path of any KServe serving-stack image.
- The remediated images build green in the existing Konflux build pipeline.
- On a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster, an InferenceService can be deployed and
  serves inference requests successfully using the remediated images.
- Serving behavior on non-FIPS clusters is unchanged, and the previously
  released image tags remain deployable as a rollback path.
- A gating CI check is wired into the KServe build pipeline and fails any
  serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): all serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters
  using validated crypto modules — KServe portion.
- HLR-3 (P1, bundled): the CI FIPS-regression gate for the KServe image
  surfaces this epic remediates. Bundled because the gate guards the same
  surfaces and shares the same detection scan as the remediation work —
  extracting it would duplicate the scan across epics and leave the remediated
  surfaces unguarded (shared-surface enforcement rule).

# FIPS 140-3 crypto remediation of Platform Operator images

## Description

This epic makes the Platform Operator images run correctly on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules, with no non-validated
crypto in the request/reconciliation path. It covers the crypto audit of the
operator images, remediation of every non-validated crypto linkage found,
verification on a FIPS-enabled cluster, and a gating CI check that prevents
regressions.

## Scope

- Audit all Platform Operator images to produce module inventory entries:
  every image, every linked cryptographic library, and its FIPS validation
  status.
- Remediate every non-validated crypto linkage: rebuild the affected operator
  images against validated cryptographic modules and FIPS-capable toolchains
  and base images.
- Rebuild and publish the remediated images through the operator's existing
  build pipeline.
- Verify operator behavior on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster: the operator
  installs and reconciles the model serving stack, with reconciliation status
  reported through the custom resource status conditions.
- Wire a gating CI check that fails any Platform Operator build that
  reintroduces non-validated crypto usage (blocking image-scan step in the
  build pipeline).
- Preserve operator behavior on non-FIPS clusters and keep previously released
  image tags deployable as the rollback path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Module inventory entries exist that list every Platform Operator image and
  each linked cryptographic library with its validation status.
- An automated scan of the rebuilt images finds no non-validated cryptographic
  library linked in any Platform Operator image.
- The remediated images build green in the operator's existing build pipeline.
- On a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster, the operator installs and reconciles the
  model serving stack successfully using the remediated images.
- Operator behavior on non-FIPS clusters is unchanged, and the previously
  released image tags remain deployable as a rollback path.
- A gating CI check is wired into the Platform Operator build pipeline and
  fails any build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage.

## Risks and Notes

- No architecture-context file is available for Platform Operator in this
  strategy's context fetch, so the operator's repo and build-pipeline
  specifics are confirmed at implementation start (implementation detail, not
  an open question — the remediation pattern is the same either way).

## HLR Traceability

  using validated crypto modules — Platform Operator portion.
- HLR-3 (P1, bundled): the CI FIPS-regression gate for the Platform Operator
  image surfaces this epic remediates. Bundled because the gate guards the same
  surfaces and shares the same detection scan as the remediation work —
  extracting it would duplicate the scan across epics and leave the remediated
  surfaces unguarded (shared-surface enforcement rule).

# FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package and certification submission

## Description

This epic assembles the FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package for the model
serving stack — module inventory, build attestations, and test results for
every serving-stack image — and shepherds it through the mandatory security
review board sign-off and submission to the external accredited certification
laboratory.

## Scope

- Consolidate the module inventory covering all serving-stack images: KServe
  components, the serving data plane, and the Platform Operator images.
- Collect build attestations for the remediated images from their build
  pipelines.
- Collect FIPS verification test results (automated image scans and
  FIPS-enabled cluster verification) produced by the image remediation work.
- Compile the evidence package in the format required by the security review
  board and the certification laboratory.
- Drive the package through security review board sign-off and submit it to
  the external certification laboratory, tracking the submission through lab
  triage.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The evidence package contains, for every serving-stack image in scope: its
  module inventory entries, its build attestations, and its FIPS verification
  test results.
- Every entry in the package traces to a specific serving-stack image and
  requirement.
- The evidence package has been signed off by the security review board,
  submitted to the external certification laboratory, and the submission has
  been triaged by the laboratory for review.

## Risks and Notes

- Certification laboratory turnaround is historically six to nine months, and
  review-board cadence is fixed — both are externally controlled and cannot be
  compressed by engineering effort. They dominate the strategy schedule and
  are recorded here as schedule risks, not as conditions on this epic's
  deliverable.
- The certification outcome and its timing are outside this epic's control;
  this epic's completion point is the assembled, board-approved, submitted,
  and lab-triaged evidence package.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): a compliance evidence package (module inventory, build
  attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security
  review board to the external certification lab.

# Document the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites

## Description

This epic authors and publishes the user-facing documentation for the model
serving stack's FIPS support: what the FIPS support posture is (which
serving-stack images run with validated cryptographic modules) and which
cluster prerequisites apply (FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters).

## Scope

- New documentation topics stating the FIPS support posture of the model
  serving stack, covering the KServe components, the serving data plane, and
  the Platform Operator images.
- New documentation topics stating the cluster prerequisites for running the
  serving stack in FIPS mode (FIPS-enabled OpenShift, validated crypto
  modules).
- Technical review of the authored content against the implemented FIPS
  behavior of the serving stack.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation states the FIPS support posture of the model serving
  stack.
- Published documentation states the cluster prerequisites for FIPS operation.
- The documentation has been technically reviewed against the implemented FIPS
  behavior, with review sign-off recorded.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster
  prerequisites.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9013: FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack

Strategy priority: Critical. Two affected components (KServe, Platform Operator),
four HLRs (P0/P0/P1/P2). Not triaged: the scope spans multiple components and
multiple distinct work streams (code remediation in two components, compliance
evidence assembly and certification submission, documentation authoring), so the
below-threshold and docs-only checks do not apply.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E001 | FIPS 140-3 crypto remediation of KServe serving-stack images | Implementation | RHOAI Serving | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E002 | FIPS 140-3 crypto remediation of Platform Operator images | Implementation | RHOAI Platform | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E003 | FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package and certification submission | Implementation | RHOAI Serving | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E004 | Document the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Docs | P0 |

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001["E001 KServe image FIPS remediation"] --> E003["E003 compliance evidence package"]
    E002["E002 Platform Operator image FIPS remediation"] --> E003
    E001 --> E004["E004 FIPS documentation"]
    E002 --> E004
    E003 --> E004
```

E001 and E002 are parallel roots (different components, different repos, no
shared artifacts). E003 consumes both remediation efforts' deliverables. E004 is
last (docs-authoring, blocked by every Implementation epic).

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 ∥ E002 (no edge) | Rule 14 | Different components and repos with no shared artifacts — the two image remediation efforts run in parallel. |
| E001 → E003 | Rule 13 (producer → consumer) | The evidence package's content — module inventory, build attestations, and FIPS test results for the KServe images — is produced by the KServe remediation work; the package cannot be assembled or submitted before those deliverables exist. This is a deliverable-content dependency on general Implementations, not a build-pipeline output consumed by a konflux-onboarding epic (no Rule 10 concern arises). |
| E002 → E003 | Rule 13 (producer → consumer) | Same relationship for the Platform Operator images: their inventory entries, attestations, and test results are inputs to the evidence package. |
| E001 → E004 | Rule 11 | docs-authoring epic is blocked by every Implementation epic in the strategy. |
| E002 → E004 | Rule 11 | Same. |
| E003 → E004 | Rule 11 | Same. |

No Investigation epics. The strategy states "None on scope" for open
questions. The one systematic unknown — which specific images link
non-validated crypto — does not change which epics exist or what they do: the
remediation epics audit, remediate, and verify the same image set either way,
handling findings fix-and-retry, and the resulting module inventory is a
deliverable of that work (feeding the evidence package). Lab scheduling and
review-board cadence are externally controlled schedule constraints, recorded as
risks on E003 — not unknowns that gate epic structure, and deliberately not
acceptance criteria.

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic(s) | Notes |
|-----|----------|---------|-------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | E001, E002 | Split by component (KServe images vs Platform Operator images), not by deferral — both halves are required for "all serving-stack images". |
| HLR-2 | P0 | E003 | Evidence package assembly, security review board sign-off, and certification lab submission. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | E001, E002 (bundled) | The CI FIPS-regression gate is a shared-surface enforcement deliverable: each remediation epic owns the gating check for exactly the image surfaces and build pipeline it converts, with the corresponding AC. Not separately schedulable — a standalone CI epic would rebuild the same detection scan over the same surfaces and leave each remediation epic's guardrail outside its scope (work-type split; contract check 6). |
| HLR-4 | P2 | E004 | Substantive new documentation topics (support posture + cluster prerequisites) — a distinct content-authoring work stream, warranting a separate docs-authoring epic. |

All four HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements.

## Health Warnings

- **Missing strategy sections**: the strategy has no Impacted Teams table, no
  Dependencies table, no Given/When/Then Acceptance Criteria, and no
  Non-Functional Requirements section. Decomposition proceeded from the HLRs
  and Affected Components; epic acceptance criteria are derived from the HLRs.
- **Team assumptions**: KServe epics are assigned to RHOAI Serving (per the
  architecture context file). The strategy names no teams, so the Platform
  Operator epic is assigned to RHOAI Platform and the documentation epic to
  RHOAI Docs as assumptions — verify with the engagement owners before
  scheduling.
- **Platform Operator has no architecture-context file** in this strategy's
  context fetch. It is treated as in-platform (it is in the canonical RHAI Jira
  component list and the strategy's premise is existing operator images linking
  crypto libraries), so no onboarding chain was generated; its
  `architecture_claims` signal is scored 0 for lack of a corroborating file.
- **"Serving data plane" scope ambiguity**: Affected Components lists only
  KServe and Platform Operator, so the serving data plane is decomposed as
  KServe's serving images. If Serving Runtimes images (vLLM, OpenVINO, Caikit)
  were intended to be in scope, additional epics under that component would be
  required — confirm with the strategy author.
- **Docs epic priority**: E004 is P0 via the docs-authoring priority exception
  (strategy priority Critical → P0) even though HLR-4 is P2. This is by design,
  not a priority inversion; E004 does not push priority onto its dependencies.
- **Epic size**: E001 and E002 may exceed the ~2-week guideline — each is one
  logical sweep (audit → remediate → verify → wire CI gate) over its
  component's image set, and splitting would duplicate the audit/detection
  mechanism across epics. Conditional re-split trigger: re-split by sub-system
  (control-plane images vs data-plane serving images) if the crypto audit finds
  materially distinct remediation approaches per image group (for example Go
  toolchain rebuilds vs Python dependency swaps) rather than the single pattern
  the strategy's "several images" phrasing implies.
- **External schedule risk** (recorded as risk, not AC, per the AC rules):
  certification lab turnaround is historically six to nine months and
  review-board cadence is fixed — both externally controlled and dominant over
  the schedule. E003's acceptance criteria stop at the engineering completion
  point the team controls: package assembled, board-approved, submitted, and
  triaged by the lab.

## Component Mapping Notes

- E003's work spans KServe and Platform Operator (the evidence package covers
  all serving-stack images); it is assigned the single most-relevant canonical
  component, **KServe**, as the serving-stack centerpiece.
- E004 uses the canonical **Documentation** component (docs-authoring work).
- E001 → KServe and E002 → Platform Operator map verbatim from the canonical
  list; no non-obvious mappings beyond the two above.

## Tiered Delivery

- **Tier 1 (independent value, not gated by the certification outcome)**:
  E001 and E002 — serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters
  (HLR-1) and CI guards against regressions (HLR-3). This is deliverable and
  valuable to public-sector deployments before any certification completes.
- **Tier 2 (externally gated)**: E003 — the certification evidence submission
  (HLR-2). Its completion timing is dominated by the accredited laboratory and
  the security review board, not by engineering speed. No upstream-PR epic is
  warranted (the strategy makes no code contribution to a third party); the lab
  is a process gate on E003's own deliverable. E004 follows the certification
  submission so the documented posture reflects the submitted evidence.
